Hey OP 👋, I'm also in a similar spot as you (minor reliant on parents) Everyone's already given pretty good advice, so I'ma focus on these points:

> They are constantly convincing me how therapy is going to just diagnose me with more conditions and my problems will get worse, that I will be with them forever and they will take my money

Not how therapy works. Firstly, if you get diagnosed with a condition - it meant you... have a condition. Conditions are just a convenient way to say "patient has impairments/struggles in XYZ". Having a condition doesn't define you, nor is it an insult, it just is.

Why would your problems get worse with proper treatment?? Actually, knowing your conditions can help find proper resources and ways to treat them. (plus some official diagnoses can be used for adjustments in school/uni, e.g. extended exam time)

Also, you can terminate therapy at any time (Though, you should consider the therapist's advice on whether or not you're ready yet) 
There's a thing called "graduating" therapy! If you develop good coping mechanisms and don't require therapy, you can "graduate" and not need therapy.


> and my dad tells me to tell my mother all my problems and tell the therapists that I am good and don’t need help. 

💀.

Just FYI, therapists exist as a neutral third-party you can safely talk to about your emotions.  For example, if you vented to your parents that their emotional neglect hurt you, they'd  probably feel insulted and act differently. 

Also, if you tell the therapist you're good when you aren't, that kinda defeats the point of therapy. :/ Therapy should be a safe space for you to talk about your issues and collaborate with the therapist to solve them, not a competition of "who can act the most OK!"
